correctness.rationale: Invariance at all cube faces; Perron functional W=l^Ty has exact negative derivative. Irreducibility forces nonzero support to spread on any hypothetical invariant zero-derivative trajectory, so LaSalle gives y->0; positive psi(0) gives z->1. Subexponential W and the stable spectral complement yield y/W->r; scalar link-deficit convolutions give (1-z_ij)/W->gamma_ij; exact derivative gives W prime/W squared -> -kappa<0. Hence tW->1/kappa. The symbolic fractions and diagnostic numerical results were reproduced from the packaged verify.py. Numerics are not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The fully inspected initiating multigroup article proves global DFE stability only for \\(\\mathcal R_0<1\\) and provides no universal critical equality profile. A previously documented scalar adaptive SIS \\(t^{-1}\\) law and a discrete metapopulation Perron \\(t^{-1}\\) law are genuine closest antecedents but have no jointly dynamic heterogeneous n-group link array. Static SIS and broad adaptive-network phase studies do not imply the gamma_ij correction by any established reduction. The contribution is the global all-n endpoint theorem with coupled leading amplitudes and the sharp response-order distinction. Priority remains conditional on unindexed literature.

value.rationale: The motivating paper resolves only strict subcritical stability and features nontrivial adaptive contact responses. At equality, the general model has a neutral epidemic mode and stable link modes, so neither threshold comparison nor static NIMFA gives the physical-time epidemic amplitude. The proof gives a global classification of all nonzero initial conditions and an explicit vector coefficient quantifying which link interventions change leading clearance speed. The linear-versus-quadratic response boundary is structurally meaningful for low-prevalence awareness modelling; the exact two-group family makes the distinction testable.
